learn.hook: △ × △ = 49 and △ + □ = 12. Can you crack the code of the hidden numbers?
points: In shape puzzles each shape hides a number. The same shape means the same number.
Use times-table facts and trial: △ × △ = 49 means △ = 7, because 7 × 7 = 49.
To make a product close to a target, try placing the bigger digits in the tens place and compare.
To count things in neat rows and columns, multiply: 8 rows of 12 chairs = 96 chairs.
Check by putting the numbers back into the puzzle.

example.q: Use the digits 3, 4 and 5 once each in ☐☐ × ☐. Which gives the biggest product?

learn.reallife: Sudoku and number puzzles in newspapers use the same guess-and-check thinking.

quiz.q: ○ × 6 = 54. What number is ○?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of thinking of the times table

quiz.q: Using 3, 4 and 5 once each in ☐☐ × ☐, which gives the biggest product?
quiz.explain: 43 × 5 = 215 beats 53 × 4 = 212 and 54 × 3 = 162. Putting the biggest digit as the single multiplier helps here.
quiz.mistake: Always puts the biggest digit in the tens place

quiz.q: Using 3, 4 and 5 once each in ☐☐ × ☐, which product is closest to 200?
quiz.explain: 212 is 12 away from 200. 215 is 15 away, 170 is 30 away.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest product instead of the closest

quiz.q: A hall has 14 rows with 16 chairs in each row. How many chairs?

A garden has 9 rows of 12 rose plants, but 4 plants are missing. How many plants are there?

learn.hook: I am odd. I am between 30 and 40. I am in the 7 times table. Who am I?
points: In a 'Which number am I?' puzzle, use one clue at a time to cross out numbers.
Some clues are useful and cut the list a lot. Others tell us nothing new.
Check your answer against every clue.
With two numbers and one operation (+, −, ×, ÷) we can make many numbers: from 4 and 5 we get 9, 1 and 20.
0 can be made as 7 − 7 or 0 × 6.

example.q: I am a 2-digit number in the 9 times table. My digits add to 9. I am less than 30. I am even. Who am I?

learn.reallife: Riddles and quiz shows use clue-by-clue thinking, just like detectives!

games.title: Make the number
items: You can make 13 from 3 and 10 with one operation.

quiz.q: I am odd, between 30 and 40, and in the 7 times table. Who am I?
quiz.explain: 7-table numbers between 30 and 40: 35 only. It is odd too.
quiz.mistake: Does not check all the clues

quiz.q: I am a multiple of 5 between 20 and 40. I am even. My tens digit is 3. Who am I?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 5 between 20 and 40: 25, 30, 35. Even: 30. Tens digit 3: 30.

quiz.q: Clues: (A) I am less than 50. (B) I am in the 10 times table. (C) I am more than 30. (D) I am a 2-digit number. Which clue is not needed?
quiz.explain: A, B and C already give only 40. Every number from them is 2-digit anyway, so D adds nothing.

quiz.q: I am a 2-digit number. I am in both the 4 and 6 times tables. I am less than 20. Who am I?
quiz.explain: In both tables and less than 20: 12 only.

quiz.q: Using 6 and 3 with one operation, which number can you NOT make?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to check all four operations

quiz.q: Which uses two numbers and one operation to make 0?
quiz.mistake: Thinks dividing a number by itself gives 0

quiz.q: Which pair with one operation makes 17?
quiz.mistake: Picks multiplication without working it out

quiz.q: Riya makes 20 using 4 and a mystery number with ×. What is the mystery number?

teach.ask: Gappu's riddle: I am in the 3 times table, I am between 10 and 20, and I am even. Which number am I? How do I solve it?
teach.praise: Both 12 and 18 fit! I need one more clue to find just one number.
teach.nudge: Which numbers are left after using each clue?

learn.hook: 60 × 50 looks big, but you can do it in one breath. Watch the zeros!
points: Changing the order of factors does not change the product: 7 × 12 = 12 × 7.
Any number multiplied by 0 is 0: 345 × 0 = 0.
× 10 moves every digit one place to the left in the place-value chart: 45 × 10 = 450. × 100 moves two places, × 1,000 three places.
For multiples of 10 and 100, multiply the basic fact and count the zeros: 60 × 50 → 6 × 5 = 30, two zeros → 3,000.
Careful: 40 × 50 → 4 × 5 = 20, then two zeros → 2,000 (three zeros in all).
learn.reallife: Shops price things in hundreds, and factories make thousands — multiplying by 10s, 100s and 1000s is everywhere.

games.title: Order and zero
items: Order does not change the product.
The digits move two places left.
Zero groups of anything is zero.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 18 × 7?
quiz.explain: Changing the order of the factors gives the same product.
quiz.mistake: Changes the digits instead of the order

quiz.q: What is 2,457 × 0?
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplying by 0 keeps the number

quiz.q: What is 45 × 10?
quiz.explain: Each digit moves one place to the left: 45 → 450.

quiz.q: What is 63 × 1,000?
quiz.explain: × 1,000 moves the digits three places left: 63,000.
quiz.mistake: Writes the wrong number of zeros

quiz.q: What is 60 × 50?
What is 40 × 500?
In a place-value chart, 342 × 100 moves the 3 from the hundreds place to which place?
quiz.explain: × 100 moves each digit two places left: hundreds → thousands → ten thousands. 342 × 100 = 34,200.

quiz.q: A carton holds 80 milk packets. How many packets are in 30 cartons?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to work out 70 × 60 quickly. What trick can I use?
teach.praise: 7 × 6 = 42, and two zeros make 4,200. Zeros are easy!

learn.hook: 16 × 25 looks tricky. But it is the same as 4 × 100! How?
points: Halve one factor and double the other: the product stays the same. 16 × 25 = 8 × 50 = 4 × 100 = 400.
To multiply by 5: multiply by 10, then halve. 48 × 5 = 480 ÷ 2 = 240.
To multiply by 25: multiply by 100, then divide by 4. 36 × 25 = 3,600 ÷ 4 = 900.
Doubling and halving helps when it makes a 10, 100 or an easy fact. It does not help much for 13 × 17.

example.q: Work out 14 × 15 by doubling and halving.

learn.reallife: Sweet-shop owners find the cost of 25 boxes quickly by thinking 'cost of 100, then divide by 4'.

quiz.q: Which is equal to 16 × 25?
quiz.explain: Halve 16 to 8 and double 25 to 50. The product stays 400.
quiz.mistake: Halves one factor without doubling the other

quiz.q: What is 48 × 5?
What is 36 × 25?
Which product is made easier by doubling and halving?
quiz.explain: 14 × 15 = 7 × 30, which is easy. The others have no handy half or double.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the trick works for every product

quiz.q: Ravi halves 18 and doubles 35. Which product does he get?
quiz.explain: Half of 18 is 9 and double 35 is 70.
quiz.mistake: Doubles and halves the same number

quiz.q: What is 9 × 70, the same as 18 × 35?
Meena buys 25 packets of chikki at ₹28 each. What is the cost?
What is 126 × 5?

teach.ask: Gappu must find 24 × 25 without a long sum. How can halving and doubling help me?
teach.nudge: What happens if I halve 24 and double 25?

learn.hook: 7 × 29? Think of 7 × 30 and take one 7 away. Done in your head!
points: Round one factor to a nearby multiple of 10 or 100, multiply, then adjust.
If you rounded up, subtract the extra groups. If you rounded down, add the missing groups.
This is useful when a factor is just 1 or 2 away from a round number, like 49, 98, 201.

example.q: Work out 9 × 48 using the nearest multiple of 10.

learn.reallife: At a shop, 4 items at ₹99 each: think ₹400 − ₹4 = ₹396.

quiz.q: What is 7 × 29?
quiz.explain: 7 × 30 = 210. 29 is one less than 30, so take away one 7: 203.

quiz.q: What is 8 × 99?
What is 6 × 51?
Which is the right way to find 9 × 48?
quiz.mistake: Takes away only 2, not 9 groups of 2

quiz.q: What is 5 × 198?
4 notebooks cost ₹99 each. What is the total?
For which product is the nearest-multiple method most useful?
quiz.explain: 99 is just 1 away from 100, so 6 × 99 = 600 − 6 is quick.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number far from a round number

quiz.q: Asha says 3 × 102 = 3 × 100 + 2 = 302. What is wrong?
options: She must add 3 × 2 = 6, so it is 306
quiz.mistake: Adjusts by 2 instead of by 3 groups of 2

teach.ask: Gappu must work out 6 × 49 in his head. What is a clever way?
teach.nudge: Which round number is 49 close to?

learn.hook: Moo! A cow at Gopal's farm gives 12 litres of milk a day. How much milk in a week? Multiplication is the fastest way!
points: Multiply when you have equal groups: 7 days of 12 litres is 7 × 12.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it into tens and ones: 24 × 15 = 24 × 10 + 24 × 5.
Price × quantity gives the total cost: 5 litres at ₹56 a litre is 5 × 56.
The order does not matter: 15 × 24 = 24 × 15.

example.q: A farm has 24 cows. Each cow gives 15 litres of milk a day. How much milk is that?

learn.reallife: Milk vans, shopkeepers and farmers multiply every day to find totals and prices.

quiz.q: A cow gives 12 litres of milk a day. How much milk does it give in 7 days?
A farm has 24 cows. Each gives 15 litres a day. How many litres in all?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only by the 5 and forgets the 10

quiz.q: Milk costs ₹56 a litre. What do 5 litres cost?
A dairy packs 36 paneer cubes in a tray. How many cubes are in 25 trays?
Meena puts 4 rows of 6 milk bottles in a crate. How many bottles are in the crate?
quiz.mistake: Adds the rows and the bottles in a row

quiz.q: Kabir's cows gave 145 litres on Monday. On Tuesday they gave double that. How much on Tuesday?
Which of these is the same as 23 × 14?
quiz.explain: Split 14 into 10 and 4. Multiply 23 by each part and add: 23 × 10 + 23 × 4.
quiz.mistake: Splits the number but multiplies only one part

quiz.q: A milk van carries 18 cans. Each can holds 40 litres. How many litres does the van carry?

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can I find the milk from 24 cows if each gives 15 litres?'
teach.praise: Moo-velous! 24 × 15: split 15 into 10 and 5, multiply, add. 360 litres!
teach.nudge: What do I do with equal groups? How can I make 24 × 15 easier?

learn.hook: Nida, Kanti and John all worked out 34 × 26 in different ways — and all got 884! Let us see how.
points: Partial products: split one number into tens and ones. 23 × 14 = 23 × 10 + 23 × 4 = 230 + 92 = 322.
Grid (area) method: split both numbers. For 34 × 26, make boxes 30 × 20, 30 × 6, 4 × 20 and 4 × 6.
Add all the boxes: 600 + 180 + 80 + 24 = 884.
Different methods are all correct if they break the numbers properly and add every part.
In word problems, look for 'rows of', 'each', 'per' to see that multiplication is needed.

example.q: A cinema has 24 rows with 35 seats in each. How many seats?

learn.reallife: Billing at a ration shop: 18 kg of rice at ₹45 a kg is a 2-digit multiplication.

quiz.q: What is 23 × 14?
In the grid method for 34 × 26, which four parts are added?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the zeros in the tens parts

quiz.q: What is 34 × 26?
Nida does 45 × 12 as 45 × 10 + 45 × 2. John does 12 × 45 as 12 × 40 + 12 × 5. Who is right?
quiz.explain: Both split a factor correctly. 450 + 90 = 540 and 480 + 60 = 540.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is only one right method

quiz.q: A theatre has 24 rows of 35 seats. How many seats?
A batter scores 48 runs in each of 12 matches. How many runs in all?
A shop bill: 18 kg of rice at ₹45 a kg. What is the bill?
A library has 36 shelves with 28 books on each. How many books?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to use the grid method for 25 × 13. Which boxes do I make?
teach.praise: Boxes 200, 60, 50 and 15 add up to 325. The grid works!
teach.nudge: How should I split 25 and 13 into tens and ones?

learn.hook: A dairy sells 312 litres of milk a day. How much in 24 days? Time for long multiplication!
points: 3-digit × 1-digit: multiply ones, tens and hundreds, carrying when needed. 234 × 6 = 1,404.
Column (long) multiplication by a 2-digit number: first multiply by the ones digit, then by the tens digit with a 0 in the ones place, then add.
3-digit × 3-digit: three rows — by ones, by tens (one 0), by hundreds (two 0s). 123 × 111 = 123 + 1,230 + 12,300 = 13,653.
learn.reallife: Factories and dairies multiply big numbers to plan how much to produce in a month.

games.title: Steps for 312 × 24
items: Write a 0 in the ones place on the next row

quiz.q: What is 234 × 6?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried digits

quiz.q: What is 312 × 24?
In long multiplication of 312 × 24, why do we put a 0 at the start of the second row?
options: Because we are multiplying by 2 tens, which is 20
To make the answer look neat
quiz.explain: The 2 in 24 stands for 20, so the row shows 312 × 20.
quiz.mistake: Treats the tens digit as ones

quiz.q: A dairy sells 312 litres a day. How much in 24 days?
What is 123 × 111?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the zeros in the second and third rows

quiz.q: What is 205 × 104?

A truck carries 250 sacks, each 48 kg. How many kg in all?

teach.ask: Gappu must multiply 213 × 32 in columns. What steps do I follow?

learn.hook: Sonu says 46 × 23 = 230. That looks too small! Can you find his mistake?
points: Always check if an answer makes sense: 46 × 23 should be about 50 × 20 = 1,000.
A common error is forgetting that the tens digit means tens: 46 × 20 is 920, not 92.
Another error: treating 200 as 20, or 70 as 7, in partial products.
Also check carrying: in 58 × 7, 8 × 7 = 56, write 6 and carry 5.
To correct an error, redo each partial product and add again.

example.q: Sonu wrote 46 × 23 = 138 + 92 = 230. Find the correct answer.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers and bank cashiers check big bills twice to avoid costly mistakes.

quiz.q: Sonu wrote 46 × 23 = 138 + 92 = 230. What is the correct answer?
quiz.mistake: Treats the tens digit as ones

quiz.q: What mistake did Sonu make in 46 × 23?
quiz.explain: The 2 in 23 is 2 tens, so 46 × 2 tens = 920.
quiz.mistake: Does not check the place value of the second row

quiz.q: Pinky wrote 312 × 200 = 6,240. What is right?
Raj wrote 58 × 7 = 356. What is correct?
Which is a quick way to see that 46 × 23 = 230 is wrong?
quiz.explain: An estimate shows the answer should be near 1,000, not 230.

quiz.q: Meera wrote 25 × 70 = 175. What is the correct product?
Kabir did 134 × 21 as 134 + 268 = 402. What is the correct answer?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the zero for the tens row

quiz.q: Which working for 27 × 15 is correct?

teach.ask: Gappu worked out 52 × 31 = 52 + 156 = 208. Something feels wrong. Can you check it?
teach.nudge: What does the 3 in 31 really stand for?

learn.hook: If you know 17 × 23 = 391, can you find 17 × 24 without multiplying again?
points: Some products are equal without working them out: 12 × 15 = 6 × 30 = 18 × 10 (all 180).
learn.reallife: Smart shoppers use 'one more' and 'one less' thinking: if 12 pens cost ₹180, 13 pens cost ₹180 + one more pen.

quiz.q: Which product has the same answer as 12 × 15, without working it out?
What is 199 × 63?
Which is the easiest way to find 16 × 25?
quiz.mistake: Does not look for a handy 100

teach.ask: Gappu knows 15 × 20 = 300. How can I find 15 × 21 quickly?
teach.nudge: How many more 15s are in 15 × 21 than in 15 × 20?

learn.hook: Red box × red box = 64. Red box × blue box = 40. What is in the blue box?
points: In colour box puzzles, boxes of the same colour hide the same number.
Find the easiest box first, then use it to find the others.
To estimate a product, round each factor to a friendly number: 48 × 21 is about 50 × 20 = 1,000.
Use estimates to choose the closest value or to check an answer.

example.q: Estimate 62 × 39 and pick the closest: 240, 2,400 or 24,000.

learn.reallife: Before paying, we estimate a bill: 9 items at ₹98 is about ₹900.

Green × 9 = 63 and Green + Yellow = 10. What is Yellow?
Blue × Blue = 36 and Blue × Pink = 54. What is Pink?
Estimate 48 × 21. Which is closest?
Estimate 62 × 39. Which is closest?
Which product is about 600?
Kavi says 52 × 49 = 548. Use an estimate to judge.
quiz.explain: 50 × 50 = 2,500, so 548 is far too small. (The exact answer is 2,548.)

quiz.q: 9 school bags cost ₹98 each. About how much do they cost?
quiz.mistake: Puts the wrong number of zeros

teach.ask: Gappu must quickly guess 41 × 29. Is it about 120, 1,200 or 12,000?
teach.praise: 41 is about 40 and 29 is about 30, so about 1,200!
teach.nudge: What friendly numbers are 41 and 29 close to?

topics.title: The King's reward and multiplication patterns

learn.hook: A clever girl asks the king for ₹1 today, ₹2 tomorrow, ₹4 the next day… doubling every day. Did the king make a mistake?
points: Repeated doubling grows very fast: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 (day 10).
Tripling grows even faster: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81. Multiplying by 5: 1, 5, 25, 125, 625.
If one factor is doubled, the product doubles: 24 × 15 = 360, so 48 × 15 = 720.
If one factor is halved, the product is halved: 12 × 15 = 180.
To find the biggest product of neighbours in a row, try each pair: big × big wins.

example.q: Reward starts at ₹1 on day 1 and doubles each day. How much on day 8?

learn.reallife: Stories of rice grains doubling on a chessboard show how fast doubling grows!

quiz.q: A reward starts at ₹1 on day 1 and doubles each day. How much is given on day 6?
Starting with ₹1 and tripling each day, how much on day 5?
Starting with ₹1 and multiplying by 5 each day, how much on day 4?
Which reward is bigger on day 10: ₹1 doubled every day, or a fixed ₹100 each day?
quiz.explain: Doubling gives ₹512 on day 10, more than ₹100.
quiz.mistake: Thinks small starts always stay small

quiz.q: Total of ₹1 doubling for 5 days (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16) is how much?

quiz.explain: 48 is double 24, so the product doubles: 720.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the product stays the same

quiz.explain: 18 is half of 36, so the product is halved: 360.

quiz.q: In the row 3, 8, 2, 9, 5, which two neighbours have the largest product?
quiz.mistake: Picks the two biggest numbers even if they are not next to each other

quiz.q: In the row 3, 8, 2, 9, 5, which two neighbours have the smallest product?
quiz.mistake: Picks the pair with the smallest single number instead of the smallest product

teach.ask: Gappu was offered 1 grain today, doubling every day for 10 days, OR 100 grains a day. Which is better on day 10?
teach.praise: Doubling gives 512 grains on day 10 — much more than 100!
teach.nudge: What do I get on day 10 if I keep doubling from 1?

learn.hook: Gopal sells milk, ghee and paneer. Every sale is a little puzzle. Let's solve them step by step!
points: Read the problem slowly. Find what is asked.
Look for clue words: 'each' and 'in all' often mean multiply; 'share equally' means divide.
Some problems need two steps. Do one step at a time.
Check that your answer makes sense.

example.q: Joseph buys 3 litres of milk at ₹58 a litre. He pays with a ₹200 note. How much change does he get?

learn.reallife: Shopping, sharing snacks and planning a picnic all need two-step thinking.

items: Each friend's part of ₹300 shared by 3

games.prompt: Put the steps for solving a word problem in order

quiz.q: A farmer gets 48 litres of milk in the morning and 36 litres in the evening. He fills 2-litre bottles. How many bottles?
quiz.mistake: Stops after the first step and gives the total litres

quiz.q: Aisha buys 4 packets of paneer at ₹85 each. She pays ₹500. How much change does she get?
quiz.mistake: Gives the cost instead of the change

quiz.q: A dairy sends 360 litres of milk each day, shared equally among 9 shops. How much does one shop get in 7 days?
quiz.explain: One shop gets 360 ÷ 9 = 40 L a day. In 7 days: 40 × 7 = 280 L.
quiz.mistake: Does only one of the two steps

quiz.q: There are 6 crates with 24 bottles in each. Which operation finds the total number of bottles?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers given instead of thinking of equal groups

quiz.q: Harpreet has ₹250. A box of ghee costs ₹65. How many boxes can she buy?
quiz.explain: 65 × 3 = 195 and 65 × 4 = 260, which is more than ₹250. So she can buy 3 boxes.
quiz.mistake: Rounds up to 4 even though there is not enough money

quiz.q: A cow eats 8 kg of fodder a day. How much do 5 cows eat in 10 days?
quiz.explain: One day for 5 cows: 8 × 5 = 40 kg. For 10 days: 40 × 10 = 400 kg.

quiz.q: 12 children share 3 boxes of 20 laddoos equally. How many laddoos does each child get?
quiz.mistake: Shares one box instead of all three

quiz.q: Kabir says: '126 ÷ 6 = 21. I can check it by working out 21 × 6.' Is he right?
options: Yes, but only for even numbers
Yes, multiplying back checks a division
quiz.explain: 21 × 6 = 126, which gives back the starting number. Multiplying undoes dividing.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that multiplication and division are opposites

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'In a story sum, how do I know whether to multiply or divide?'
teach.praise: Wonderful! Equal groups to find a total means multiply. Sharing equally means divide!
teach.nudge: What clue words tell me to multiply? Which words tell me to divide?

learn.hook: 156 litres of milk must go into 12-litre cans. How many cans? Division will pour it out neatly!
points: Divide to share equally or to make equal groups.
144 ÷ 6 means: share 144 into 6 equal parts, or how many 6s are in 144.
If it does not share exactly, the extra is the remainder. The remainder is always smaller than the number you divide by.
Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = the number you started with.

example.q: 156 litres of milk is poured into cans of 12 litres. How many cans are filled?

learn.reallife: Dairies pack milk into equal packets. Teachers share sweets equally on Children's Day.

items.text: The remainder must be ___ than the number we divide by

games.title: True or false?
items: 4 × 7 = 28, so the remainder is 1. A remainder of 5 is too big when dividing by 4.
Dividing a number by 1 leaves it the same.
Sharing nothing among 5 gives each 0. So 0 ÷ 5 = 0.

quiz.q: A dairy has 144 litres of milk. It fills 6 cans equally. How much milk goes in each can?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts or multiplies instead of dividing

quiz.mistake: Adds or subtracts 12 instead of dividing

quiz.mistake: Leaves a remainder bigger than 8, or ignores the leftover

quiz.mistake: Makes a slip with the tens
